```{python}

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
```

## QUESTION 1

1. __Create a new 'season' column.__ Define 'season' as:
    1. Winter for January, Febuary (note the mispelling), March
    1. Spring for April, May, June
    1. Summer for  July, August, September
    1. Fall for October, November, December
    1. All other rows can be assigned a value of 'Unknown' 

_No discussion needed for this question_

```{python}
# Q1: Add season column using when/then chaining

df = df.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("month").is_in(["January", "Febuary", "February", "March"]))
    .then(pl.lit("Winter"))
    .when(pl.col("month").is_in(["April", "May", "June"]))
    .then(pl.lit("Spring"))
    .when(pl.col("month").is_in(["July", "August", "September"]))
    .then(pl.lit("Summer"))
    .when(pl.col("month").is_in(["October", "November", "December"]))
    .then(pl.lit("Fall"))
    .otherwise(pl.lit("Unknown"))
    .alias("season")
)

# Verify the season mapping
df.select(["month", "season"]).unique().sort("month")

```

## QUESTION 2

1. __Divide all the columns by 1000 whose name starts with num_of.__ Be sure to first filter out rows that contain problematic values for the columns like -999 or 1500+.

_No discussion needed for this question_

```{python}
# Q2: Clean and scale num_of columns

# Identify columns starting with 'num_of'
num_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith("num_of")]

# Build a filter mask that excludes rows where any num_of column
# contains problematic values (-999 or "1500+")
mask = pl.lit(True)
for col in num_cols:
    mask = mask & ~pl.col(col).cast(pl.Utf8).is_in(["-999", "1500+"])

df = df.filter(mask)

# Cast all num_of columns to Float64 (they may still be strings)
df = df.with_columns([
    pl.col(c).cast(pl.Float64) for c in num_cols
])

# Now divide them by 1000
df = df.with_columns([
    (pl.col(c) / 1000).alias(c) for c in num_cols
])

# Show sample of scaled columns
df.select(["airport_code", "month"] + num_cols[:4]).head(5)

```

## QUESTION 3

1. According to the BTS website, the “Weather” category only accounts for severe weather delays. Mild weather delays are not counted in the “Weather” category, but are actually included in both the “nas” and “late_aircraft” categories. __Using the columns you modified in the bullet above, your job is to create a new column that calculates the total number of flights (in 1,000's) delayed by weather (both severe and mild).__ Show your work by printing the first 5 rows of the dataset. Use these three rules for your calculations:  

    a. 100% of delayed flights in the Weather category are due to weather  
    a. 30% of all delayed flights in the "late_aircraft" category are due to weather  
    a. From April through August, 40% of delayed flights in the NAS category are due to weather. The rest of the months, the proportion rises to 65%  

_No discussion needed for this question_

```{python}
# Q3: Calculate total weather delays

# Define the month condition for April through August
april_to_aug = pl.col("month").is_in(["April", "May", "June", "July", "August"])

df = df.with_columns(
    (
        pl.col("num_of_delays_weather") +                          # 100% weather
        pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft") * 0.30 +             # 30% late aircraft
        pl.when(april_to_aug)
        .then(pl.col("num_of_delays_nas") * 0.40)                  # 40% NAS (Apr-Aug)
        .otherwise(pl.col("num_of_delays_nas") * 0.65)             # 65% NAS (rest)
    ).alias("total_weather")
)

# Print first 5 rows with relevant columns
df.select([
    "airport_code", "year", "month",
    "num_of_delays_weather", "num_of_delays_late_aircraft",
    "num_of_delays_nas", "total_weather"
]).head(5)

```

## QUESTION 4

1. __Using the new weather variable calculated above, create a boxplot showing the distribution of flights delayed by weather for each season. Describe what you learn from this graph.__    

Winter shows the highest median weather-related delays and the largest spread, with many extreme outliers. Spring also has elevated delays. Summer and especially Fall have noticeably lower medians and tighter distributions. If you want to avoid weather delays, Fall months (October–December) appear to be the best choice, while January through March are the riskiest.

```{python}
# Q4: Boxplot – total weather delays by season
(
    ggplot(df, aes(x="season", y="total_weather"))
    + geom_boxplot(fill="lightblue", outlier_color="red")
    + labs(
        title="Distribution of Weather-Related Flight Delays by Season",
        x="Season",
        y="Total Weather Delays (thousands of flights)"
    )
    + theme_minimal()
)

```
